risks.title: Tariffs
risks.score_rationale: Tariffs imposed by the United States on products imported from China, Canada, and Mexico could increase raw material and sub-assembly costs. Masimo operates in the United States, Mexico, and Malaysia with critical supply chains from China and Southeast Asia. The company is actively mitigating these risks through supply chain adjustments and exemption requests, but the duration and magnitude of tariffs remain uncertain.

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The medical technology market is highly competitive. Masimo has achieved significant market share gains through contract acquisitions, particularly with hospital customers, but remains exposed to increased competition to maintain its position.

risks.title: Cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: The company has previously experienced a cybersecurity incident resulting in costs and disruptions. Masimo's connectivity and remote monitoring solutions represent critical targets. The company must continue to invest substantially in cybersecurity.

risks.title: Geopolitical Risk
risks.score_rationale: The Russia-Ukraine, Israel-Palestine, and Iranian-related conflicts could impact regional operations. Masimo remains compliant with applicable U.S. and European sanctions but actively monitors these risks.

risks.title: Regulatory Risk
risks.score_rationale: Regulatory changes, including tariffs, regulatory approvals for monitoring technologies, and compliance with international standards, represent ongoing operational risks.

risks.title: Technology Dependency
risks.score_rationale: Masimo relies heavily on proprietary technologies (SET pulse oximetry, rainbow CO-oximetry) and hospital automation platforms for its competitiveness. Technological obsolescence or critical disruptions expose the company.

risks.title: Supply Chain Disruptions
risks.score_rationale: Masimo experienced major installation challenges in 2023-2024 due to hospital labor shortages and delivery delays from OEM equipment suppliers (GE Healthcare, Philips, Hillrom). While 2025 performance is encouraging, bottlenecks persist.
